title: Stream preview hot paths and remove extraction hash overhead
description: Bounded performance slice under TSK-0008 / TSK-0065. Current user-supplied editor logs show steady-state generation dominated by FieldSampling (~387-408 ms) and AppearanceBake (~189-196 ms), with optimized MeshExtraction usually ~113-117 ms and occasional contour-resolution variance. Implemented three behavior-preserving reductions: row-oriented Burst SDF sampling removes per-sample flat-index division/modulo and reduces scratch to one row; streamed Burst appearance resolution removes the vertexCount × programCount distance matrix while preserving absolute-distance and Body tie semantics; direct integer grid corner/edge ownership replaces the extraction Dictionary<long,int> with deterministic dense ownership tables and overflow guards. Acceptance requires Unity parity/determinism/topology validation and fresh benchmark measurements before marking complete.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Implementation round 2026-09-10: DensityGrid.SamplePortable now uses row-oriented Burst sampling with bounded per-work-item scratch isolation and contiguous x traversal. AppearanceBaker routes nearest appearance selection through the consolidated AppearanceResolveBurst streamed candidate reducer instead of a full distance matrix and merge pass. MarchingCubesExtractor now uses GridVertexOwnership with direct integer corner/X-edge/Y-edge/Z-edge slots and owner+1 sentinel encoding. Existing AppearanceBakerTests already contain Bake_BurstResolve_MatchesManagedResolveExactly; existing extraction tests cover watertightness and welding invariants. Unity test execution and fresh benchmark comparison remain pending in this environment.

comments.author: user
comments.body: User-supplied Quality 16 steady-state editor logs: TotalGeneration 701.9, 700.6, 798.8, 720.5, 702.8 ms; FieldSampling 386.8-407.5 ms; MeshExtraction 112.6-208.9 ms, normally ~113-117 ms except one 208.9 ms run driven by MeshContourResolution 147 ms; MeshValidation ~5 ms; AppearanceBake 188.7-196.0 ms. Mesh output was stable at 20,962 triangles / 10,483 vertices. These measurements are the post-threading-fix baseline supplied by the user and should be compared with the new implementation after Unity warm-up.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Review correction before validation: the first row-batching implementation shared one scratch buffer across parallel work items, which could race. The current implementation allocates bounded per-work-item scratch slices (RowsPerExecute chosen under an 8 MB budget) and offsets each row into its own slice. The unsafe version is no longer the branch state.
